title: test_role_absent_demand_inert double-frees the aliased trimmed demand-entries array
evidence:
529: 	trimmed := make([dynamic]Demand_Entry, 0, 4, context.allocator)
530: 	defer delete(trimmed)
...
537: 	delete(e3.entries)
538: 	e3.entries = trimmed
catalog.odin:982: 		delete(cat.demand.eras[i].entries)
detail: defer delete(trimmed) frees the backing array; defer catalogs_destroy(cat2) then deletes the aliased eras[2].entries — same allocation freed twice. odin test core logs '+++ bad free @ 0x42A001478 [catalog.odin:982:catalogs_destroy()]' for this test; a standalone tracking-allocator repro panics.
recommended_fix: Drop 'defer delete(trimmed)' — ownership transfers to cat2 (catalogs_destroy frees it once). Or trim e3.entries in place via resize instead of aliasing a second array.

title: W9 hosts>=8 assert vacuously satisfied by the 14 pre-seeded streaming terminals
detail: The re-pin seeds 14 streaming-capable terminals before tick 1, so hosts>=8 passes by construction; the 'growth must place the aggregation crowd' pin silently stopped biting on a growth regression (previously one seeded host forced growth to supply the crowd).
recommended_fix: Count only growth-born streaming terminals (exclude the seeded ids) or assert hosts > 14 so the check reflects the seeded fixture.

title: W9 EXPECTED hardcodes the surge volume (20) while deriving only the window from data
evidence:
630: 	surge := &cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces[0]
631: 	SURGE_START := u64(surge.start_tick)
632: 	SURGE_END := SURGE_START + surge.duration_ticks
633: 	WINDOW := SURGE_END - SURGE_START // the active window [start, start+duration)
634: 	EXPECTED := 20 * WINDOW // the doubled ask: 2 streaming entries × ×10 × WINDOW
detail: No guard that surge.multiplier == 10 or that exactly two era-3 streaming entries exist; a multiplier/entry-count re-tune silently desyncs MIN_LAND from the honest ask — the drift class the 'cannot silently drift this pin' comment claims to prevent.
recommended_fix: Compute EXPECTED from data: sum era-3 streaming-entry volumes × surge.multiplier × WINDOW, or assert surge.multiplier and the streaming-entry count.

title: test_terminal_class_profiles hardcodes the surge window split, unbounded at the end
evidence:
445: 	SURGE_AT :: u64(1200) // the streaming surge's data start_tick
...
448: 		in_surge := tick >= SURGE_AT
detail: Unlike W9, the base/surge split is not derived from the set piece, and in_surge has no end bound; if start_tick or duration_ticks is re-tuned (duration < 800), post-surge ticks silently pollute per_role_surge and skew the ratio pins.
recommended_fix: Derive SURGE_AT/SURGE_END from cat.demand.eras[2].set_pieces (start_tick + duration_ticks) exactly as test_w9_surge_lands_under_caps does.
